P1.evidence: The application was acknowledged but deliberately not read back — 'So I went through the application that you left us. So I have a somewhat of an understanding what you're going through. But I'm kind of an old school guy. So I would love to hear it from you.' That is a defensible choice but it is not the scripted move, which exists so the prospect feels seen. No four-part frame and no frame agreement. The open question ran cleanly: 'What, what actually brought you to the call?'

P2.evidence: The injury probe is the best in this batch and was earned rather than lucky — the rep pattern-matched the trade first ('I met a lot of guys from the tile industry, and a lot of them, they had either knee injuries, pain back issues. Is that the same case with you?'), then followed with 'Where does it show up right now?' and 'Do you encounter that right now when you wake up and when you're laying down?' and 'Are you taking any medications, like painkillers or something like that?'. Work was explored properly, including the physical load and the travel pattern. Height and weight were both asked directly; age never was. Health conditions were only approached through the medication question — no direct or hereditary-conditions question, and the father's decline was volunteered. The real failure is sleep and energy: this prospect has severe chronic sleep disruption and volunteered all of it unprompted ('I don't remember the last time I got a full, like eight hours of sleep'), and the rep never asked either question, so both score as misses under the volunteered-information rule. P2f is N/A — he has no current training to have produced results.

P3.evidence: The depth was reached, but the prospect walked there himself and the rep mostly asserted rather than asked. The bridge was delivered as a leading statement — 'From what I'm hearing, and I get that a lot with the guys that I speak to... Most of them that have that big why behind why they want to do it is for their families, basically. And that's also your case, yeah?' — which the script asks as an open question. Same with the impact question: the sons and the father at 70 came from the prospect. What the rep did do well is P3g and P3h. He drove all the way through to legacy — 'you're going to be that 70 year old that you cannot move by yourself. You need somebody helping you, right?' — and delivered a clean reflect-back at 00:26:16: 'this doesn't sound like a motivation problem at all... The problem is that you just don't have a structure built around your actual life.' The prospect immediately took ownership of that frame.

P4.evidence: One well-aimed question did most of the work: 'you've been an athlete, so you know the drill. You know you've been disciplined. How do you think? What's the missing piece between then and now that you weren't able to pick it up, right?' The prospect gave a structured two-part answer — time-balance with his wife, and exhaustion — and then named the real gap himself: 'what's been holding me back is I don't have anybody really to hold me accountable... I need a coach, man. That's what I'm missing.' The root-cause frame was reinforced with the athlete analogy rather than the scripted line ('when you're an athlete, everybody is taking care of your nutrition, your programming... But then you're on your own'). Prior specific attempts were never inventoried — the training-with-friends story was volunteered and not followed up.

P5.evidence: The consequence was delivered as a statement rather than asked as a question: 'you're in this spot that it's very easy to fall off and just like, ah, forget it. And then you're going to be that 70 year old that you cannot move by yourself.' It landed — the prospect had already supplied the raw material with his father — but he was never made to say the cost in his own words, never asked whether he would settle for it, and never asked to draw a line in the sand. Notably the prospect's own consequence material was the strongest in the batch and the rep used it to build rapport rather than to build pressure.

P6.evidence: The prospect pre-empted the phase by asking for the price at 00:42:57, and the rep let that stand in for the scripted questions. P6a appeared only in inverted form — 'the only way you don't get results in this program is if you choose not to show up, but based on everything you told me, that's not who you are, right?' P6b was started and abandoned: 'I actually wanted to ask you about commitment. Are you committed to showing up, but actually, you just, you just said that, that you want to do that.' A clear yes did exist before the price ('I'm ready, man. I have to do this, not just for myself, the why behind it, my family, for my kids, for my wife. They are my why'), so P6c holds, but it was volunteered rather than obtained.

P11.evidence: Step 2 was done and done early — six Trevor slots read out and Wednesday 2:15pm Mountain booked. Step 1 failed after a hard push: the Paiva application would not verify the prospect's phone and PayPal financing declined him, so no money was collected and payment now rests on a text message once a house sale clears. Step 3 was never touched — no agreement email, no signature. Step 4 only partially: Skool was described, but as a post-programme community perk rather than an onboarding action, and no welcome email or onboarding questionnaire was mentioned. Worth flagging as a sequencing issue that the onboarding call was booked before payment was secured, which is the reverse of the scripted order and left a Trevor slot held against an unpaid deal.

objection_plays.detail: Only the isolation move ran — 'just to make sure that we're on the same page. Like, you're not in a... Should I do it?' — and the prospect confirmed he was in. Everything else was skipped in favour of lending. No 'most clients pay upfront but for some we break it up', no permission question about an honest financial conversation, and none of the six financial-picture questions: cash on hand, monthly surplus, number of cards, available credit, used versus available, investments. Given the prospect had just volunteered that a large sum was landing in his account within forty-eight hours, one question about the timing would have closed this cleanly without a credit application.

Script gap — a solvent buyer with a dated liquidity gap. The prospect was not saying he could not pay or that it was the wrong time; he was saying the money arrives on Tuesday. The playbook only distinguishes capacity from no capacity and offers nothing for a forty-eight-hour deferral, so the rep improvised by refusing the deferral and routing to third-party credit. That produced a declined application and no revenue, where waiting two days would very likely have produced $6,000 in cash.

Script gap — clinical fit, and the most consequential instance of it in this batch. The prospect disclosed progressive spinal pain with a new radicular symptom while under active physiotherapy. There is no scripted screening or clearance step, and rather than leave it, the rep advanced a mechanistic counter-explanation and positioned strength work against the clinician's approach: 'a lot of people are saying, oh, I'm stiff, I need to stretch a lot. No, you need to get stronger.'

notes: Genuinely strong on discovery mechanics — the injury probe and the reflect-back at 00:26:16 are both worth using as training examples — and the rep was honest where he could have upsold, actively recommending six months over twelve. Three corrections. First and most important: when a prospect is under a clinician's care for a progressive spinal problem, that is a stop-and-ask moment, not a place to offer an alternative theory of his back. Second, P5 was skipped as a phase even though the prospect handed over perfect consequence material about his father; making him voice it would have cost nothing. Third, the payment sequence inverted the process — the Trevor call was booked before the money, a twenty-four-hour deferral from a man closing on a house was refused, and two credit applications were run instead, one of which was declined. Roughly eighteen minutes of the call were spent troubleshooting payment rails.
